name: Latin American, Caribbean, and Latinx Studies
notes: Five courses plus a language prerequisite. Course lists come from the department's minor course-list PDF (sas.rochester.edu/lacx/assets/pdf/lacx-minor-courses.pdf), not from the minor page itself.
DIVISION IS DETERMINED BY YOUR COURSEWORK: 'The division of the minor (humanities or social sciences) will be that in which the student takes three courses.' Filed here under humanities.
For a course to qualify, roughly 50 percent of its content must relate to Latin America.
Up to two study-abroad courses may count with the approval of your minor advisor, and the minor must be approved by the designated program coordinator.

PETITIONS: a student may petition for a course not previously identified as a Latin American studies course by submitting its syllabus; the program coordinator decides whether it counts as listed or requires specific Latin America-related research.

There are currently NO approved LACX clusters; the page recommends Indigenous Studies (S1INT021), Hispanic Film and Popular Culture (H1SP003), Literature and Identity in Hispanic Societies (H1SP001) and Latin American History and Culture (S1HIS019) instead.

requirementGroups.label: Prerequisite: Spanish or Portuguese through the 152 level
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Prerequisite: Students must complete SPAN 151 and 152, SP 153, or PORT 151 and 152. Students who are placed in SPAN 200 may use that course as their language prerequisite.

requirementGroups.label: Five Latin American, Caribbean and Latinx studies courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: A total of five courses related to Latin American and Caribbean people and their diasporas, their languages, and their cultures are required for the minor. Two courses must be taken from different areas, such as anthropology, business, economics, history, international relations, political science, Portuguese, religion, or Spanish.
requirementGroups.note: Two of the five must come from different areas - the planner cannot check that spread.
